subject: Crestpoint pilot: eval scope, dataset format, and scoring
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jensen <laura@crestpoint.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: eval goals, recommended models, and dataset checklist

Thanks for taking the call this morning, Laura — good to meet you and Mike. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can kick the pilot: 

1) Goal (what Crestpoint wants to validate)
- Automating triage for inbound patient intake messages and extracting structured fields (problem, urgency, insurance status) with >85% entity-level recall and high-priority routing accuracy.

2) Recommended model candidates to bench on Redwood (initial shortlist)
- redwood-open-7b-quant (fast, cost-efficient for high throughput)
- redwood-13b-v2 (better higher-context extraction; slightly higher cost)
- instruction-tuned-11b (safety/structured-output preference)

3) Benchmark assets I uploaded (see attachments + Drive link)
- crestpoint_eval_template_v2.csv: expected CSV schema (id, text, labels_json, metadata)
- crestpoint_prompt_bank_sample.md: seed prompt permutations + expected answer format examples
- Shared Drive folder: full scoring rubric and sample scoring sheets

4) Scoring & quality guardrails
- Primary metrics: field-level F1 (per entity), and routing precision@top1 for urgent cases
- Secondary: hallucination checks (label mismatch rate), and a human-accept rate for borderline outputs
- Proposed human-in-the-loop cadence: 200-shot manual review at start, then weekly drift checks

5) Action items we agreed on
- Laura / Mike: share a de-identified sample of ~500 rows (CSV, match attached schema) by 2026-12-06
- Redwood: provision the evaluation bucket and upload scoring template (I attached crestpoint_eval_template_v2.csv)
- Stakeholders: confirm final scoring rubric and who will be the two Crestpoint scorers (names + emails) by next Wed

6) Timeline
- Get sample and confirm rubric: by 12/06
- Redwood runs initial bench (3 model variants) and returns pilot report: target 12/13

Notes on security/data retention you asked about: short answer, we can run the eval under your VPC or using dedicated project isolation; I'll loop Security for specifics once you share the sample.

Attached: crestpoint_eval_template_v2.csv; crestpoint_prompt_bank_sample.md; MAP_Crestpoint_Mini.docx

If that lines up, reply-all with the sample ETA and names of your scorers and I'll create the HubSpot tasks and shared Drive permissions.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com | (415) 555-0129

From: Laura Jensen <laura@crestpoint.com>

Thanks, Nikhil — this is helpful and matches our internal notes. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can deliver a de-identified sample (500 rows) by 2026-12-03 rather than the 6th; would that work?
- Scorers: I will nominate two clinical reviewers (Laura K. and Omar) by EOD Monday (11/30).
- Important: we need confirmation on data retention and access logs for the evaluation. Can Redwood provide the SOC2 evidence and a short note on how long eval artifacts will persist if we use the hosted route?

On procurement: we may need a minimal DPA amendment for the pilot. Who should our procurement team contact?

Regards,
Laura Jensen

Looping in a quick ops note — happy to own the scoring configuration and run the initial bench.
- I'll provision an eval project and set up a read-only bucket for Crestpoint samples (retention = 30 days by default for pilots; we can extend or run in VPC if needed).
- Proposed scorer workflow: two Crestpoint reviewers for adjudication + one Redwood reviewer for mismatch debugging.
- I'll also prepare a small scoring guide (2 pages) that maps columns in crestpoint_eval_template_v2.csv to scorer UI labels.

Nikhil: I'll need the sample and final scorer emails to finish provisioning.

—Ben

ben_carter@redwood.com

Great — thanks, everyone. Confirmations and next steps: 

- Laura: sample by 2026-12-03 is perfect. Please send as CSV matching attached schema and strip PHI. If you prefer SFTP, Ben will share details.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.
